title: Helios Retail Labs - Activation Standup & Infra Intake
summary: Intro standup to align infra connectivity, data residency, and pilot scope for Helios' recommendation engine; agreed next steps to run a small inference benchmark on private deployment and share security pack. Some audio dropouts in the middle, a few mis-transcribed acronyms.
action_items: Dana Ortiz: Provide VPC CIDR and service account (due: 2027-01-03)
Jordan Li: Run 1-day benchmark on Redwood Private with 2x A10G equiv nodes and share perf sheet (due: 2026-12-30)
Priya Desai: Share onboarding checklist, security pack, SOC 2 attestation doc link (due: 2026-12-23)
Benji Alvarez: Confirm KMS provider and key rotation policy (due: 2027-01-07)
next_steps: Redwood to provision staging tenant for Helios and schedule benchmark run
Helios to share network details and minimal dataset for end-to-end latency test
Schedule 30-min technical deep-dive next week to review benchmark results
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 10:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM); Dana, Benji, Sofia (Helios)
Links shared: onboarding checklist (redwood.com/docs/helios-onboard), perf sheet (tinyurl.com/redwood-bench-xyz)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Good morning everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we want to run through infra intake and confirm pilot success criteria.
[00:23] Dana (Helios): Morning, Dana here. We have Benji and Sofia as well. Excited to get this moving.
[00:31] Maya: Awesome. Priya from success will take notes for the runbook. Jordan will lead the benchmark and infra questions.
[00:44] Jordan (Redwood SE): Hi all — quick note: we'll be targeting Redwood Private for the pilot unless you prefer Dedicated; we discussed pros/cons earlier but we want to make sure the network egress and KMS story fits your security needs.
[01:05] Benji (Helios): Our preference is Private — we want the control plane but data in our VPC, yes. We use AWS KMS and rotate keys quarterly.
[01:18] Jordan: That's fine. We integrate with customer-managed KMS; we will need the key ARN and a service account with encrypt/decrypt permissions. Also, VPC peering or PrivateLink? Which do you want?
[01:35] Benji: Prefer PrivateLink for tighter control, but we might do VPC peering depending on networking team. I'll check.
[01:42] Maya: Action: Benji to confirm PrivateLink vs peering with CIDR.
[01:48] Sofia (Helios): One other question — tokenization and latency: our average prompt is around 200 tokens, spikes to 800 for aggregated user history. Can Redwood handle that without large latency impact?
[02:05] Jordan: Yes — runtime supports dynamic batching and KV cache for prefix reuse. For the pilot we'll pin a model and test two quantization profiles: q4f16 and q8_0 to measure tradeoffs. We'll show per-token latency and cost delta in the perf sheet.
[02:28] Dana: Great. On compliance: we need SOC 2 Type II reports and audit logs retained for 12 months. Also SSO via SAML for admin access.
[02:45] Priya (Redwood): We have SOC 2 doc and an audit-log export mechanism. I'll drop the attestation and a sample audit-log schema in the onboarding packet. SAML SSO is supported; we need the IdP metadata.
[03:00] Maya: Noted.
[03:07] Jordan: For benchmarks, recommend two runs: 1) 24-hour steady run at 50K queries/day to measure cost and throughput; 2) tail-latency stress at burst QPS to see p99 behavior. We'll simulate your prompt distribution.
[03:27] Benji: 50K/day matches expected production (after ramp). What hardware are you thinking for Private?
[03:36] Jordan: We'll propose a 2-node A10G-equivalent pool with autoscale policy set to maintain 95% SLO for median latency, and a burst buffer for peak. If cost is a concern we can try an A10+V100 mix.
[03:52] Maya: Clarify cost vs latency tradeoff will be in the perf sheet; Jordan will annotate.
[03:58] Sofia: One more — data residency: some shopper PII must remain in EU. Our platform spans NA and EU. Can Redwood route EU traffic to the EU region only?
[04:14] Jordan: Yes, smart routing by region is supported. We'll configure a regional policy and mark EU datasets accordingly. For Private we'll ensure nodes are provisioned in the EU region.
[04:28] Dana: Good. Also, logging and analytics — we want per-route token cost breakdown and traced requests for debugging.
[04:40] Priya: That's part of Console — token-level breakdown and tracing hooks can be enabled per environment. We'll show sample dashboard.
[04:51] Benji: Network question — do you require an internet-facing endpoint? We're air-gapped for some environments.
[04:58] Jordan: For Private we offer an optional on-prem package. If fully air-gapped we'll need an offline bundle and an installer; that's a separate process and timeline. For this pilot, linking via PrivateLink/VPC peering should suffice.
[05:17] Dana: Okay we don't need full air-gap yet.
[05:22] Maya: Logistics — timeline and success criteria. Dana, what are your must-haves to call the pilot successful?
[05:31] Dana: Must-haves: p50 latency < 180ms for 200-token prompts, p95 < 500ms; cost per 1K tokens under our threshold (we'll add a number in the doc); private KMS integration and SOC 2 certs.
[05:47] Jordan: We will instrument metrics to show p50/p95 and include cost extrapolation.
[05:52] Sofia: Stakeholders: we'll have product and infra leadership sign off; timeline target is beta by end of Q1.
[06:02] Maya: Good. We'll aim to have initial benchmark results in a week if we get network details today.
[06:09] Benji: We might need an approval for service account creation; I'll escalate.

[audio drop: ~40s silence — partial transcription gap]

[12:10] Jordan: Picking up — thanks for that. Back to kv cache: for the 800-token history spikes we'll enable prefix caching to reduce re-compute; that helps tail latency significantly. We'll document cache hit ratio impact.
[12:35] Benji: Any observed regressions with quantized models on long context? We worry about generation quality.
[12:42] Jordan: We'll run quality checks with your prompt set; q8 config tends to preserve quality better than aggressive q4, but cost differs. We'll attach a small eval harness and a comparison report.
[13:05] Dana: Sounds good. Also, will Redwood accept our customer-supplied model or do we need to use a model in Redwood's catalog?
[13:15] Jordan: Private supports self-hosted models; we can load your custom model artifact as long as it conforms to the loader format. We'll provide the packaging guide.
[13:27] Sofia: Perfect. We'll try a small distilled model first.
[13:33] Maya: Next — incident response: what SLAs do you need in pilot?
[13:39] Dana: 1-hour for P1, 4-hour for P2 during business hours.
[13:45] Priya: We'll align on an SLA addendum; for Dedicated we have SLA-backed targets — for Private we can include an agreed-upon response cadence. I'll draft a short SLO doc.
[13:58] Benji: Security: we also need key rotation proof and ability to revoke keys quickly if compromised.
[14:05] Jordan: KMS integration supports rotation. For revocation, we can revoke access and rotate keys; we'll show the flow in the runbook.
[14:15] Dana: Excellent.
[14:20] Maya: Ok a couple of practical items — I'm going to send the pricing ballpark and the onboarding packet to your team after the call. Priya will attach the SOC2 and audit doc. Jordan will schedule the benchmark run once Benji shares network details.
[14:36] Sofia: Timeline for benchmark scheduling?
[14:39] Jordan: If we get VPC details today, we can provision staging and run the benchmark by 12/30. It will be a 24-hour run, results by 12/31.
[14:51] Benji: We'll try to get you the network details by EOD tomorrow.
[14:56] Dana: I have a question about rate-limiting and quotas — can we enforce per-API-key quotas? We want to throttle internal services differently than external ones.
[15:08] Jordan: Yes, rate-limiting and quotas are per-token/per-route; we can set per-key policies and tie to RBAC roles.
[15:18] Maya: Cool. Any other blockers?
[15:21] Dana: No blockers besides networking and KMS confirmation.
[15:25] Sofia: One minor note — our security team requested a pen-test schedule; do you do third-party pen tests or provide a testing window?
[15:36] Priya: We do third-party pen tests on the control plane; for Private we can coordinate a controlled window. I'll note contact points.
[15:46] Benji: On observability — we want a light-weight trace id passed back on API responses so our debugging correlates with our logs.
[15:56] Jordan: We return a request-id and can propagate trace headers. We'll show examples in the API spec.

[31:02] Maya: Ok we'll recap and action items. Jordan — benchmark run, Priya — docs and SOC2, Benji/Dana — network details and KMS.
[31:15] Jordan: I'll run perf with two quant profiles, attach CSV with p50/p95 and cost est.
[31:22] Priya: I'll upload the onboarding checklist now and share link in the meeting notes.
[31:28] Dana: Thanks, that helps.
[31:32] Sofia: Do we have a date for the technical deep dive to go through results?
[31:36] Maya: How about next Tuesday 09:00 PST?
[31:40] Benji: Works for us.
[31:42] Dana: Works.
[31:45] Maya: Great. Final note — one of the questions that tends to come up is fallback policies: if a model variant is down, we can automatically route to a compatible variant. That can be part of your resiliency plan.
[31:58] Jordan: We'll include an example config for rollouts/canaries and auto-fallback.
[32:06] Benji: Nice.
[32:09] Maya: Alright thanks everyone. Priya will follow up with links and next steps.
[32:16] Dana: Thank you.
[32:19] Sofia: Thanks all.
[32:21] (call ends)
